title: John, again
tomorrow: the council calls Peter and John ignorant men. why can't it stop them?

segments.voice: A week of looking back down the mountain: the night taught, a true self under the costume, here I am, out of egypt, justice and mercy, and yesterday, the father runs. Six carries. Today, one word that holds them.

Houseplants have their own apps now: reminders to water, to turn the pot toward the light. But cut a stem off and no app can save it. At the Last Supper in John's Gospel, Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "I am the vine: you the branches." A branch doesn't strain to make grapes. It has one job. It stays on.
screen: `AN APP FOR YOUR PLANTS.` → `I AM THE VINE: YOU THE BRANCHES.` → `ONE JOB: STAY ON.`

segments.voice: The word for that job is abide. "Abide in me, and I in you." It means stay, remain, make your home in. John uses the same idea at the very start of his Gospel. Two people follow Jesus and ask where he's staying. He says come and see, and they stay with him the rest of that day. The first thing anyone does with Jesus in John is not work. It's stay. Now hold the week up to that vine. The night taught because John of the Cross stayed in the dark instead of leaving prayer. Merton's true self is found by staying still long enough to drop the costume. Here I am is abiding said out loud. Out of Egypt was a walk toward a home with God. Justice and mercy is what grows on a branch that stays put. And the father runs toward a son coming back to the vine. One word under six carries: abide.
screen: `ABIDE IN ME, AND I IN YOU.` · `COME AND SEE; THEY STAYED.` · `SIX CARRIES ON ONE VINE.` · then, large: `ABIDE.`

segments.voice: Find one steady sound: a fan, traffic, your own breathing. Stay with it, the way a branch stays on the vine. When your mind wanders off, come back to the sound; that coming back is abiding.
John. The Gospel of the vine and the branches, and one plain word: abide.
Hold on to this: abide, like a branch that simply stays on the vine. Week done, rest well.
